newsitem.title: USA: Kurzweil execs barred from boards - SEC.
newsitem.headline: Kurzweil execs barred from boards - SEC.

text.p: The former chief executive Kurzweil Applied Intelligence and two ex-vice presidents agreed to a consent decree barring them from serving as an officer or board member of any public company, the Securities and Exchange Commission said Wednesday.

Ex-CEO Bernard Bradstreet and vice presidents Thomas Campbell and Debra Murray, consented, without admitting or denying guilt to a final judgement that also bars them from any future violations of the antifraud provisions of the securities law, SEC Assistant Director for Enforcement Grant Ward said.
Action is still pending against a fourth defendant, former vice prsident David Earl, who is scheduled to go to trial in October.

The consent decree, which seeks no financial redress, stems from a complaint filed against the Massachusetts-based hi-tech firm and its executives that inflated Kurzweil's revenues and earnings and sold shares in the company knowing the financial statements were false, the SEC said.

In addition to the SEC complaint, U.S. Attorney for Massachusetts Donald Stern filed criminal indictments against both Bradstreet and Campbell who were subsequently found guilty of five counts of conspiracy, securities fraud and falsification of corporate records. The pair are to be sentenced on the criminal convictions Oct 22.
Ward said the SEC did not seek reimbursement or assess penalties against the men because Bradstreet and Campbell have "demonstrated an inability to pay."
The consent decree must still be approved by a federal judge.
